column3: The Hebrew uses a verb of speaking or meditating upon the wonders; BSB says tell.
The Hebrew has a singular heart; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew names the judgments of His mouth; BSB describes judgments He pronounced.
The Hebrew shifts from singular you to plural your inheritance and names a measuring cord; BSB does not mark the number shift.
The Hebrew’s second destination is another people, not another kingdom; BSB says from one kingdom to another.
The Hebrew names breaking every staff of bread; BSB says cutting off supplies of food.
The Hebrew has a singular foot and says his soul came into iron; BSB has feet and placing his neck in irons.
The Hebrew names his word coming and the LORD’s utterance refining him; BSB describes a prediction coming true and proving him right.
The Hebrew says binding princes; BSB says instructing them.
The Hebrew leaves the actor unnamed and says He made His people stronger than their foes; BSB names the LORD and says more numerous.
The Hebrew has a singular heart; BSB has hearts.
The Hebrew explicitly names words of His signs; BSB says miraculous signs.
The Hebrew explicitly says they did not rebel against His word; BSB says they defied His words.
The Hebrew names the chambers of their kings; BSB says royal chambers.
